callout.text: A fisherman in the North Atlantic

explainedBy: Renewable vs nonrenewable limits begin with a North Atlantic fisherman and his trawler.

storyboard.claim: To examine limits, picture a fisherman in the North Atlantic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The bearded fisherman in yellow oilskin beside a fishing trawler at sea.
storyboard.onScreenText: A fisherman in the North Atlantic
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New section: from delays to limits.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the fisherman and the trawler the passage keeps.

explainedBy: The fisherman works the freezing deck of a commercial factory trawler: a tough job.

storyboard.claim: He stands on the freezing deck of a factory trawler; a tough job.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman and trawler; his face turns strained, shoulders hunched in the cold.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; walk becomes a cold hunch.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the boat as an industrial factory trawler.

explainedBy: The trawler's winches haul up miles-long drift nets from a cold churning sea.

storyboard.claim: Hydraulic winches haul up miles-long drift nets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The trawler icon hauling its net, the fisherman pointing at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the net-hauling becomes the subject.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the icon already shows a net; the callout adds its scale.

callout.text: The very last schools of cod

explainedBy: The fisherman hunts down the very last scattered schools of cod: the catch is running out.
noVisual: no sonar screen in the vocabulary; the fish he hunts carries the claim

storyboard.claim: He stares at sonar, hunting the last scattered schools of cod.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fisherman pointing at a fish: the target of the hunt.
storyboard.onScreenText: The very last schools of cod
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the boat to what he is hunting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that the fish themselves are now scarce.

explainedBy: Every reinforcing loop hits a constraint; the fisherman has reached his: the fish are running out.

storyboard.claim: He is hitting a limit; no physical system grows forever.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman and fish; he slumps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; point becomes slump - the hunt meets the wall.
storyboard.addedInformation: The body shows the limit being hit.

explainedBy: Weighing the two kinds of limit: renewable or not.
noVisual: the two kinds of limit are introduced as words; the next beats picture each

storyboard.claim: The system's fate depends on whether the constraint is renewable or not.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weighing the two kinds of limit: renewable or not.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From one fisherman to the general rule. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: sets up the contrast drawn next.

explainedBy: An oil field is the classic nonrenewable resource: the stock itself is the limit.

storyboard.claim: An oil field is stock-limited: the stock is the limit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An oil pumpjack pumping oil.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First side of the contrast: nonrenewable.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pictures the oil field the claim is about.

explainedBy: All the oil that will ever exist sits underground, finite; the pump takes it out as fast as machinery allows.

storyboard.claim: The whole amount is underground, finite; you pump it as fast as machinery allows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same pumpjack keeps pumping.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout names the finite stock.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the pump shows extraction; finiteness is in the text.

explainedBy: The faster you extract the oil, the faster it is gone: it does not regenerate.

storyboard.claim: The faster you extract it, the faster it is gone - a countdown.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same pumpjack, labelled as a countdown.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the consequence of pumping.
storyboard.addedInformation: States that extraction speed sets how soon it ends.

explainedBy: Fish, unlike oil, are a biological renewable resource: they reproduce.

storyboard.claim: Fish are a renewable resource: they reproduce.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fish replaces the oil pump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The contrast flips: oil -> fish.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pictures the renewable side.

explainedBy: If you only catch fish at the speed they make new fish, the fishery is limited by that flow.

storyboard.claim: A fishery is flow-limited: catch only at the speed they regenerate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fish.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the rule for the renewable side.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the rule is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: Respecting the regeneration rate lets you harvest indefinitely: the limit is the flow, not the stock.

storyboard.claim: You can harvest indefinitely; the limit is the regeneration, not the total stock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fish, labelled forever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the payoff of respecting the flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts 'forever' with the oil countdown.

explainedBy: The challenge: technology - better sonar, bigger nets, onboard freezers - lets the fleet keep catching more.

storyboard.claim: Human ingenuity is boundless: better sonar, bigger nets, onboard freezing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fisherman cheerfully pointing at his trawler.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the boat, now as the optimist's argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the tools the argument relies on.

explainedBy: With boats out for months the industry keeps growing, on the assumption the fish keep breeding.

storyboard.claim: Boats stay out months; the industry keeps growing because fish keep breeding.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman and trawler; he celebrates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; point becomes celebrate - the growth story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the optimism being argued.

explainedBy: 'A technology problem, not a limit problem' is rejected: that assumption destroyed the Newfoundland cod fishery.

storyboard.claim: It's a technology problem, not a limit problem - a deadly assumption that destroyed the Newfoundland cod fishery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman; the celebration drops into a slump; the claim struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the optimist's phrase is rejected.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike shows the host rejects the claim.

explainedBy: A reinforcing loop: profit buys bigger boats, which catch fish faster than they can breed.

storyboard.claim: Profit buys bigger boats in a reinforcing loop, catching fish faster than they breed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: profit -> bigger boats -> faster catch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rejected claim to the mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause -> effect chain the narration names.

explainedBy: Catch outpaces breeding, but the objection is that the fish still breed.

storyboard.claim: It catches fish faster than they can breed - but they still breed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fisherman beside a fish, arguing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the loop to the objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the objection lives in the callout.

explainedBy: Driven down and down, the fish population falls below a threshold where they can no longer find mates.

storyboard.claim: Biology has tipping points: below a critical threshold they cannot find mates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman and fish; he slumps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; talk becomes worried slump.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the tipping point.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: the population drops below the threshold and the food web collapses.

storyboard.claim: Or the food web collapses, or predators take their niche.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman and fish; fear replaces worry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; more ways the population fails.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the mechanism itself is only in text.

explainedBy: Crossing that line turns a renewable resource into a non-renewable one: the renewal mechanism breaks.

storyboard.claim: Crossing that line turns a renewable resource into a non-renewable one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman and fish; sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the result of crossing the line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links back to the oil countdown.

explainedBy: When extraction outpaces regeneration and delays hide it, the result is overshoot and collapse.

storyboard.claim: Extraction outpacing regeneration, with delays, gives overshoot and collapse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: extraction outpaces -> overshoot -> collapse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the threshold to the book's model.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the whole chain at once.

explainedBy: After the collapse the fish are gone and the trawlers rust at the docks.

storyboard.claim: Total wipeout; the fish are gone; trawlers rust at the docks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fisherman slumped beside his idle trawler.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the model back to the boat - now idle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the consequence for the same man and boat.

explainedBy: Fishing towns go bankrupt: the system destroys itself by being too good at its job.

storyboard.claim: Fishing towns go bankrupt; the system destroys itself by being too good at its job.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same fisherman, now sitting by the trawler.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; slump becomes sitting idle.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the paradox of efficiency.

explainedBy: Not bad luck: a reinforcing loop, growing like a snowball, hits a flow-limited resource whose threshold we ignore.

storyboard.claim: It's not bad luck - a reinforcing loop hits a flow-limited resource and we refuse to respect the threshold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A snowball rolling and growing: the reinforcing loop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the result to its cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pictures the runaway loop as the cause.

explainedBy: If runaway loops destroy their own resources, the question is how anything survives.

storyboard.claim: If systems are so prone to collapse, a terrifying question follows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same growing snowball.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; from cause to question.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the question is in the callout.

explainedBy: The host asks why everything hasn't already collapsed.

storyboard.claim: Why does anything survive at all?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host asking, surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question spelled out.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a host asking.

explainedBy: The properties that keep healthy systems alive, sorted.
noVisual: abstract properties; no icon reads as resilience

storyboard.claim: Healthy systems have three properties, resilience and hierarchy among them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The properties that keep healthy systems alive, sorted.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: names the properties as text.

explainedBy: Resilience starts with your commute: driving through a hyper-efficient single-lane tunnel.

storyboard.claim: You drive through a hyper-efficient single-lane city tunnel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman seated, commuting on a road.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New example: the commute.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the viewer on the road.

explainedBy: The algorithm spaces the cars perfectly: a driver's dream.

storyboard.claim: Traffic flows beautifully, cars spaced perfectly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same everyman, now happy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the start state - smooth flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the satisfied driver.

explainedBy: The car ahead hits debris and gets a flat tire: one small shock.

storyboard.claim: The car three lengths ahead gets a flat tire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same driver, startled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; happy -> surprised: the shock.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the flat tire itself is only text.

explainedBy: Brake lights flare, horns blare, and within 90 seconds the tunnel is jammed.

storyboard.claim: Brake lights, horns, within 90 seconds total gridlock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same driver, angry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; surprise turns to fury.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the driver's escalating reaction.

explainedBy: Infuriating gridlock: the tunnel was perfectly efficient but had zero resilience.

storyboard.claim: Gridlock: perfectly efficient, but zero resilience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same driver, slumped, stuck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the end state - stuck.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the lesson of the example.

explainedBy: The most efficient system sits at the fragile end: no slack in the line.
noVisual: efficiency-vs-fragility is abstract; the tunnel already showed it

storyboard.claim: The most efficient system is the most fragile: no slack in the line.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The most efficient system sits at the fragile end: no slack in the line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalizes the tunnel. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.

explainedBy: In pursuit of hyperefficiency we strip away idle resources and emergency buffers.

storyboard.claim: We strip away idle resources and emergency buffers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An executive cutting, papers in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From principle to the people doing the cutting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows cutting as a business decision.

explainedBy: We slash extra warehouse inventory to run just-in-time global supply chains.
noVisual: no warehouse icon; the factory stands in for the supply chain

storyboard.claim: We slash warehouse inventory to run just-in-time supply chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A factory: the industrial supply chain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First example of a buffer cut.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the inventory cut is in the text.

explainedBy: We cut sleep to work more hours, and pave wetlands for condos, because buffers look like waste.

storyboard.claim: We cut sleep to work more; pave wetlands for condos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped at his desk beside a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second example: the personal buffer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows lost sleep for work.

explainedBy: The three buffers - inventory, sleep, wetlands - are not idle: they provide resilience.

storyboard.claim: Those buffers aren't idle; they provide resilience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: the three buffers named.
storyboard.onScreenText: Warehouse inventory -> 8 hours of sleep -> Muddy wetlands
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gathers the examples.
storyboard.addedInformation: Groups the three buffers as one kind of thing.

explainedBy: Buffers absorb shocks; remove them and the first shock - a pandemic, a flu, a hurricane - hits.

storyboard.claim: Remove buffers and the first shock - a pandemic, flu, hurricane - arrives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A storm: the shock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From buffers to what they protect against.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pictures the hurricane named.

explainedBy: Without buffers, the shock destroys the system; healthy systems are also hierarchical.

storyboard.claim: The shock destroys it. Healthy systems are also hierarchical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same storm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the result.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the outcome.

explainedBy: Hierarchy builds from the bottom up: cells form organs, organs form bodies.

storyboard.claim: They build from the bottom up: cells form organs, organs form bodies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: cells -> organs -> bodies.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New property: hierarchy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the bottom-up structure.

explainedBy: Hierarchy built from the bottom up: bodies form communities.

storyboard.claim: Bodies form communities; hierarchy handles the flow of information.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hierarchy built from the bottom up: bodies form communities.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: One level up the chain. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.

explainedBy: If every cell talked to every other cell at once, you would explode from information overload.

storyboard.claim: Every cell talking to every cell would mean exploding from overload.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman cowering, overwhelmed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the principle to its absence.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: shows overwhelm, not the cells.

explainedBy: The objection: hierarchy in human society is about the top controlling the bottom.

storyboard.claim: Wait - hierarchy in human society is about control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The objection: hierarchy in human society is about the top controlling the bottom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection begins. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a host objecting.

explainedBy: The objection's picture: the CEO at the top dictates orders down to the factory workers.

storyboard.claim: The CEO at the top dictates orders down to the factory workers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO pointing at the factory worker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection made concrete.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows top-down command between two people.
